title: Human-approved Project Map delivery
summary: A user opens a dedicated owning-workspace Agent session for a scoped brief, follows its visible Draft and Production validation, reviews a candidate, approves its exact fingerprint, and exports verified artifacts.

chapters.title: Human intent and delivery
chapters.summary: The user chooses scope and a launcher, edits the request, explicitly opens a fresh Agent tab, and sees each known startup and work milestone.

chapters.title: Agent authoring and validation
chapters.summary: The selected Agent uses the local contract, updates repository-owned source, and reports Draft then Production validation.

chapters.title: Approval and export
chapters.summary: EZTerminal presents semantic and evidence changes, locks approval to one Production fingerprint, and exports only that approved map.

steps.label: Open guided Project Map creation
steps.detail: The empty state exposes one explicit action and states that EZTerminal will request, not author, repository files.

evidence.claim: The empty state opens guided creation while explicitly retaining manual authoring and the no-app-write boundary.

steps.label: Inspect approved map and evidence
steps.detail: An existing map remains searchable and evidence-backed before the user requests a selective update.

evidence.claim: The inspector supports directed exploration, exact evidence navigation, and named verification checks.

steps.label: Choose map type and new-session Agent
steps.detail: Creation is limited to native map types and configured Codex or Claude launchers; an already-active or coordination-joined Agent is not required.

evidence.claim: The form loads configured launchers and admits only Codex or Claude for Project Map work.
The guided form exposes the closed map-type selector, new-session Agent selector, exact workspace hint, and editable brief before launch.

steps.label: Review and edit the scoped brief
steps.detail: The visible brief defines schema v2, semantic layout intent, evidence, Draft and Production checks, and the no-auto-commit boundary.

evidence.claim: Creation instructions require repository-owned schema v2 source, evidence, semantic-only layout intent, both quality profiles, and human review.

steps.label: Open a dedicated Agent session
steps.detail: EZTerminal validates the exact project, root, workspace, and launcher, then opens and focuses a fresh terminal through the normal New session path.

evidence.claim: The explicit action prepares the exact owning workspace and hands a runtime-only Project Map request to a new Agent terminal.
The Project Map navigation callback routes the validated bootstrap and project session into a new workbench terminal and reports whether it opened.
The normal workbench path registers the bootstrap before adding a fresh terminal pane and clears it if pane creation fails.

steps.label: Bind a persisted job to the fresh activity
steps.detail: After observing the new terminal's exact session and provider, EZTerminal records collection, intent, activity, dedicated dispatch, Agent label, and queued phase.

evidence.claim: Dispatch ignores older activities, waits for the exact fresh session and provider, then starts the job with that activity and dedicated-session metadata.
The main-owned store persists activity and dedicated-session identity, enforces one active job, ordered progress, and explicit cancellation.

steps.label: Submit the tracked brief in the new PTY
steps.detail: The new terminal embeds the persisted job ID and reporting contract, submits the brief once through its ready-aware PTY path, and cancels the new job if submission fails.

evidence.claim: The helper creates the final job-bound prompt, submits it once, and cooperatively cancels the just-created job if submission throws.
The fresh Agent terminal dispatches the Project Map request through its own BlockController and retains an in-tab retry path for startup or queue failure.

steps.label: Show truthful request progress
steps.detail: Persistent saved, dedicated-session, and Agent-work milestones show only known progress, plus intent, phase, update time, job ID, and cooperative Cancel.

evidence.claim: The global request strip derives exact copy and three milestones from durable dispatch and phase data, exposes timestamps and cancellation, and preserves a compatibility fallback for older jobs.

steps.label: Load the native authoring contract
steps.detail: The Agent reads a closed local guide instead of importing external schemas, code, or generated output.

evidence.claim: The capability-bound Agent endpoint returns the repository-native guide only for a closed Project Map type.

steps.label: Update authoritative typed source
steps.detail: The Agent changes the manifest or impacted map spec and evidence in its dedicated owning-workspace session.

evidence.claim: Existing-map authoring names the owned source, preserves portability constraints, and opens a fresh exact-workspace Agent session only from an explicit handler.

steps.label: Run Draft validation
steps.detail: Draft gives the Agent a named quality profile and structured diagnostics before the final gate.

evidence.claim: The native shim validates guide, Draft or Production check, and job phase arguments without a system Node dependency.
The loopback check accepts an explicit Draft or Production profile and returns verification, provenance, or structured diagnostics.

steps.label: Pass Production validation
steps.detail: Production requires current inputs, exact evidence, deterministic layout, ten passing checks, clean diagnostics, and resolved provenance.

evidence.claim: ProjectMapService validates source, evidence, authoritative inputs, deterministic scene, named checks, provenance, and caches only a clean Production document.

steps.label: Keep approved map live and show candidate
steps.detail: An approved cache opens immediately while one coalesced Production verification prepares an exact candidate and semantic/evidence diff.

evidence.claim: Background verification is single-flight and builds a candidate, last-approved display source, approval state, and stable-ID semantic/evidence diff.

steps.label: Review candidate changes and evidence
steps.detail: The human sees verification banners, semantic and evidence changes, source anchors, and all named checks while the persistent job strip remains above the surface.

evidence.claim: The request status is mounted above empty, creation, and diagram content whenever a persisted job exists.
Candidate, last-approved, verification, and stale banners precede the semantic and evidence diff.
Selected claims expose directed exploration, exact evidence, and every named verification check in the native inspector.

steps.label: Approve the exact Production fingerprint
steps.detail: Approval is enabled only for a valid Production candidate with every check passed and no diagnostics.

evidence.claim: The renderer derives candidate readiness from Production quality, valid state, zero diagnostics, and all passing checks before sending its fingerprint.
Main revalidates the exact fingerprint and Production gate, saves approval, and completes an awaiting-review job only after approval.

steps.label: Export canonical verified artifacts
steps.detail: The app exports SVG, 1600 by 900 PNG, and a verification receipt from the approved canonical scene into a new fingerprinted directory.

evidence.claim: The UI selects a destination and exports only the currently approved map ID and fingerprint with an explicit theme.
Export rejects authoritative directories, stages canonical SVG, PNG, and receipt without overwrite, then atomically renames the fingerprinted folder.
The primary empty-state action changes only the local guided-creation state.
Existing maps expose a separate explicit update brief that opens the same dedicated owning-workspace Agent path.
Type and Agent selection precede the editable creation brief in one visible form.
The launch control requires a supported Agent and safe non-empty brief, validates the exact target, and opens a fresh-session bootstrap only in its click handler.
The request waits for a live activity matching only the new terminal session and selected provider before persisting the job.
The delivered prompt carries the job ID and the ordered analyzing through awaiting-review reporting contract.
A prompt submission failure immediately cancels the just-created queued job rather than leaving a false waiting state.
Starting, canceling, and Agent-reported job changes update the cached snapshot and emit a collection-scoped change for the persistent status strip.
The Agent can retrieve the native map-type contract through its scoped loopback capability.
The brief directs the Agent to inspect authoritative implementation and add exact evidence before writing claims.
The native CLI accepts a map ID with an explicit Draft quality profile and rejects invalid arguments locally.
Draft and Production are closed request values passed to the same main-owned validation service.
Invalid evidence, stale inputs, layout errors, or provenance errors return diagnostics and prevent a clean Production cache entry.
The scoped Agent reports validating-production then awaiting-review against the persisted job.
Candidate state and semantic or evidence change counts are presented before approval.
Approval appears for an unapproved candidate, while export controls stay disabled until an approval fingerprint exists.
Approval is offered only for an unmatched candidate, while both export controls stay disabled until an approved fingerprint exists.
